The “CR” icon on LinkedIn images: what it shows and how to remove it

Noticed a small “CR” badge in the corner of an image you posted on LinkedIn? It means the file carries Content Credentials, and anyone can click it to see where the image came from. Here is what it reveals and how to post without it.

Updated 2026-11-26 · 4 min read
Short answer: The CR icon appears when the image or video you upload has C2PA Content Credentials. Clicking it shows details from that record, such as the app used, sometimes a name, and whether generative AI was involved. LinkedIn only shows what is in the file: remove the Content Credentials with IA Cleaner before uploading and the icon won’t appear.

What the CR icon can reveal

  • The app or tool that created or edited the image: Photoshop, Firefly, ChatGPT, a phone camera with Content Credentials…
  • A name or account, if the creator’s app attached one.
  • Whether AI was used, for example “generated with AI” or “edited with AI”.
  • Dates and actions recorded in the manifest.

It is useful when you want to prove where an image comes from. It is a problem when a client presentation, a portfolio piece or a profile picture shows more than you intended.

Post without the CR icon

  1. Open IA Cleaner → Images (or Video for MP4 or MOV).
  2. Drop the file and check the box What the original reveals: it shows the same kind of information LinkedIn would.
  3. Download the clean copy and upload that one.

Cleaning is lossless: the image looks exactly the same. Nothing is uploaded to IA Cleaner.

Already posted?

The icon comes from the file that was uploaded, so the only way to remove it from a post is to upload a clean copy again. If you want to keep Content Credentials on purpose — to show your work is authentic — simply don’t clean the file.

What IA Cleaner detects and removes

In photos (JPG, PNG, WebP) it identifies and removes GPS location, camera and phone model, dates, editing apps, XMP and IPTC data, C2PA Content Credentials and embedded AI prompts. Pixels and colour profile stay the same. You see the full report first — every block found, with AI-related ones flagged — and then download the clean copy.
